reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about the effects of an FCC additive on strain, transformation reversibility, hysteresis, and heat transfer in FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoribbons, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises.
premises: FCC metal additive (e.g., Pd) promotes local structural relaxation and reduces interfacial strain in FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs
Reduced interfacial strain improves magnetic ordering and fosters a more reversible martensitic/magnetostructural transformation
More reversible transformation leads to reduced magnetic hysteresis and enhanced magnetocaloric effect
Microstructural refinement from the additive improves heat-transfer in nanoscale geometries
These effects persist under low-applied-field, heat-transfer-limited cycling in nanoribbons/thin films
